versions.changelog: Listing card states the account precondition. Verified against production: only restaurant lookup/search and general dietary questions work without a linked hello.food account; every profile-reasoning and household tool refuses. Names where accounts are created (the app, or heyfood register — there is no web signup) and that linking uses a phone number rather than an email. Skill content is unchanged from 1.0.6.
Clarify host-owned OpenClaw compatibility and preserve exact Codex/Claude remediation.
Add exact disclosure handoff guidance for v0.8 household reads while preserving the v0.7 human-TUI path.
Discover household capabilities from the installed manifest; preserve truthful v0.7 TUI handoff and enable only advertised v0.8 read tools.

explain_item is not menu-grounded and is not a cold-menu fallback. It assesses the item NAME against the dietary profile and never reads a captured menu, so restaurant_name is context rather than evidence. After a menu_not_captured result an agent must not quietly retry with explain_item and present the answer as though it came from the restaurant's menu. The name/id asymmetry is no longer framed as a convenience shortcut.

Household scope guidance for both surfaces. Hosted: the default is household-wide rather than the owner; member_id=_self does NOT narrow to the owner (only an explicit household_scope=_self does); evaluate_menu headline status is the household aggregate with member_annotations saying who; 422/404 scope rejections must never be retried unscoped or fallen back to the owner. Local: householding in client 0.7.0 is human-TUI only — no household capability, command, or MCP tool — so an agent must route the user to the terminal app rather than attempt it.

Restaurant, menu and recipe workflow guidance. Setup command now requests the six required scopes and the read-only tool filter — without them no scopes are granted and every authenticated tool refuses. Manifest compatibility gates on fields rather than a version number, so a client manifest bump no longer disables the local surface. Corrects what get_menu_status answers: it polls a job you started, not whether a menu exists.

heyfood 1.0.0

- Initial release supporting restaurant/menu safety evaluation, dish explanation, recommendations, and recipes via remote hello.food tools.
- Adds support for dietary profile reading, household-aware Grocery reads/exclusions, and Menu Watch reads on local hey.food MCP server.
- Clearly distinguishes local and remote MCP surfaces, with separate, non-overlapping capabilities and tools.
- Enforces strict safety, consent, and mutation boundaries—no automation of human TUI and no bypassing human-only approvals.
- Provides detailed guidance on authentication, authority, and food safety context preservation.
